body.x: ZOOC participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12.

ZOOC operates the ‘Fitapat’ platform, which allows users to customize characters based on their beloved pets. The company identified the needs of consumers who want to consume characters created by their loved ones. They defined that traditional ‘customization,’ hindered by technical limitations and cost barriers in producing desired products, often needs to be consumed. ZOOC aims to normalize ‘customization’ by addressing these issues.

Operating under this vision, fitapat uses eight photos to create over 80 concept characters of pets using AI. The platform significantly reduces design costs by 95% compared to traditional methods and reinvests these savings in product quality. fitapat focuses on providing high-end custom products to customers.

At CES 2024, ZOOC introduced a prototype allowing users to create custom dog designs. They also exhibited actual production goods, enabling attendees to confirm the quality of the products and demonstrate the system through videos.

ZOOC mentioned, “We are receiving proposals from companies that want to collaborate using our characters. Some companies in the education content sector expressed interest in creating educational content using our characters. Companies developing pet-specific displays and CCTV have also proposed collaborations to customize our AI characters. Customizing pets into characters seems to attract much interest.”

In addition, ZOOC stated, “In 2024, we plan to focus on launching collaborative products with other companies and expanding sales through offline store placements. Technologically, we will concentrate on automating the entire process of custom product production, establishing a physical production equipment system, and stabilizing the technology. Currently, we are limited to producing around 40 high-end products per day, but we aim to build infrastructure to produce up to 1,000 products through our efforts.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
